title: Python for Government Data Analysis
description: Covers Python fundamentals, data cleaning, exploratory analysis and basic visualization using government datasets.

title: SQL for Government Databases
description: Introduces relational databases, SQL queries, joins, filtering, aggregation and basic database reporting.

title: Machine Learning Fundamentals for Public Services
description: Introduces supervised and unsupervised learning, model evaluation and practical use cases in government data analysis.

title: APIs and System Integration
description: Covers REST APIs, authentication, data exchange and basic integration of government applications and services.

title: Cloud Computing Fundamentals for Government
description: Introduces cloud concepts, virtual machines, storage, databases, deployment models and basic cloud security.

title: Data Engineering Fundamentals
description: Covers data pipelines, ETL processes, data storage, transformation and preparation of data for analytics.

title: Software Development Practices for Government Applications
description: Covers software design principles, version control, testing, documentation and maintainable application development.

title: Cybersecurity for Software Developers
description: Introduces secure coding, common application vulnerabilities, authentication, access control and security testing.

title: Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals
description: Provides an introduction to AI concepts, machine learning, generative AI and responsible use of AI in public services.

title: Data Visualization with Python
description: Covers transforming datasets into charts and dashboards and selecting appropriate visualizations for government reporting.

title: Introduction to DevOps
description: Introduces version control, continuous integration, continuous delivery, automated testing and deployment concepts.

title: Web Application Development Fundamentals
description: Covers web application architecture, backend services, databases, APIs and basic application deployment.

title: Cybersecurity Awareness for Officials
description: Covers common cyber threats, phishing, password security, safe device use and incident reporting for government personnel.

title: Data Privacy and Protection in Government
description: Introduces principles of data protection, responsible handling of personal information, access controls and privacy-aware workflows.

title: Digital Signatures and Electronic Records
description: Explains digital signatures, electronic records, authentication and secure digital document workflows in government.

title: e-Governance and Digital Public Services
description: Covers principles of e-governance, digital service delivery, citizen-centric design and interoperability.

title: GIS for Government Applications
description: Introduces geographic information systems, spatial data, mapping and practical applications for planning and public administration.

title: Digital Identity and Authentication
description: Covers digital identity concepts, authentication methods, authorization and secure access to government services.
targetGroup: IT Officers and Digital Service Teams

title: Open Data and Data Sharing in Government
description: Introduces open data principles, data publishing, metadata, data quality and responsible inter-departmental data sharing.

title: Responsible Use of Generative AI in Government
description: Covers practical uses of generative AI, prompt design, verification, confidentiality, bias and responsible deployment considerations.

title: Digital Accessibility for Public Services
description: Introduces accessibility principles for government websites, documents and digital services to improve inclusive access.
targetGroup: Digital Service Teams and Content Managers

title: Blockchain Fundamentals for Public Administration
description: Provides a basic overview of distributed ledgers, blockchain architecture, use cases and limitations in public-sector systems.
targetGroup: Government IT Officers and Policy Professionals

title: Information Security Management Basics
description: Introduces information security policies, risk assessment, asset protection, access management and incident response.

title: Digital Service Design for Citizens
description: Covers user needs, service journeys, usability testing and iterative design of citizen-facing digital government services.
targetGroup: Government Programme Managers and Digital Teams

title: Effective Communication in Public Service
description: Develops clear written and verbal communication skills for interaction with citizens, colleagues and senior officials.

title: Effective Leadership in Public Service
description: Covers leadership styles, team direction, accountability, delegation and decision-making in public-sector environments.

title: Problem Solving and Decision Making
description: Introduces structured problem-solving, root-cause analysis, evidence-based decisions and evaluation of alternatives.

title: Teamwork and Collaboration
description: Focuses on collaboration, role clarity, conflict management and effective coordination across government teams.

title: Ethics and Integrity in Public Service
description: Covers ethical decision-making, integrity, accountability, conflicts of interest and professional conduct.

title: Time Management and Workplace Productivity
description: Introduces prioritization, planning, workload management and practical methods for improving workplace productivity.

title: Negotiation and Stakeholder Management
description: Develops skills for identifying stakeholder interests, negotiating solutions and managing professional relationships.

title: Presentation Skills for Government Officials
description: Covers structuring presentations, explaining technical information clearly, visual support and delivery techniques.

title: Emotional Intelligence at the Workplace
description: Introduces self-awareness, empathy, emotional regulation and interpersonal skills for effective workplace interactions.

title: Change Management in Government
description: Covers organizational change, stakeholder concerns, communication strategies and practical approaches to implementing new processes.

title: Critical Thinking for Public Policy and Administration
description: Develops skills in evaluating evidence, identifying assumptions, comparing alternatives and forming reasoned conclusions.

title: Stress Management and Resilience at Work
description: Introduces practical approaches to workload management, resilience, workplace pressure and maintaining effective professional performance.

title: Index Numbers and Price Statistics in India
description: Covers sources of data, status and limitation of price statistics; concepts, methodology and construction of WPI, CPI and development indices (SDI, HDI); compilation of Index of Industrial Production (IIP).

title: Social Statistics
description: Concepts and definitions of social statistics; human development and socio-economic indicators; gender statistics; vital statistics; health, education, labour and housing statistics; poverty measurement and multidimensional poverty index.

title: National Accounts Statistics
description: Theoretical concepts of social, national and environmental accounting; estimation of national income and related aggregates (GDP, saving, capital formation, private consumption expenditure); preparation of income estimates from primary, secondary and tertiary sectors; input-output analysis.

title: Sampling Methods and Techniques used in Large Scale Sample Surveys
description: Review of sample survey techniques; survey planning, frame and selection of sampling scheme, sample size; questionnaire design; post-survey operations, field and computer scrutiny; estimation procedure and multipliers; report writing with practical experiences from NSSO, NFHS, RCH and SRS surveys.

title: Demography and Population Studies
description: Concepts of mortality, fertility and morbidity; construction of life tables and population projections using Mortpak and Spectrum software; population policy, family welfare, RCH and NRHM; impact of population growth on poverty, gender, urbanisation and employment.

title: Training of Trainers (TOT) - Index Numbers and Price Statistics
description: Training of trainers programme on price statistics covering WPI, CPI, development indices and compilation of IIP, aimed at senior officials of State DES and faculty of State Training Institutes.

title: Training of Trainers (TOT) - National Accounts Statistics
description: Training of trainers programme for senior officials of State DES and faculty of State training institutes on concepts, sources of data and estimation of national accounts statistics and GDP aggregates.

title: Planning and Designing of Large Scale Sample Surveys
description: Review of sample survey techniques; survey planning, frame and selection of sampling scheme, sample size; questionnaire design; post-survey operations including field and computer scrutiny, multipliers and report writing; surveys using network and quota sampling.

title: Handling Large Scale Data & Data Analysis using R
description: Practical orientation to data analysis in R including descriptive analysis, regression, logistic/log-linear analysis, factor and cluster analysis; handling unit level data of NSSO including understanding multipliers and estimation procedures.

title: Big Data Analysis
description: Data science and concept of big data; data-driven decision making, data visualization, predictive analytics, data mining techniques, forecasting, survival and cluster analysis, linear and logistic regression; optimization using R, SAS, SPSS and Excel.

title: Poverty Analysis and measuring Inequality
description: Definition of poverty, prevalence and estimates; measuring poverty, income inequality and poverty line estimation; use of NSSO data for poverty measures; poverty alleviation programmes in India and their impact.

title: Labour Force and Employment Statistics
description: Labour market trends and segmentation; concepts related to labour force and employment; underemployment, working poor, informal and unpaid work; sources of data and national and international practices in compiling labour statistics.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Concept of Block Chain
description: Artificial intelligence and machine learning; attacks in virtual world and mitigation approaches; usage of blockchain technologies in land records; disruptive technologies in today's world with focus on official statistics.

title: Communication Skill Development
description: Goals for specific communications, the communication process, one-on-one and group communication, barriers to effective communication; influencing techniques; planning a communication strategy; face-to-face and virtual facilitation skills.

title: Python Training for Statisticians
description: Python commands, lambda functions, tuples, lists, dictionaries, file operations, modules and packages, exception handling; packages for data science including numpy, pandas, matplotlib and seaborn; data pre-processing and model building with sci-kit learn.

title: Data Analysts and Data Ware House
description: Concepts of data warehousing, tools and ETL; schema modeling, designing and developing dimension and fact tables; entity-relationship modeling using ERwin and generating SQL scripts.

title: Advanced Sampling Techniques with practical examples from NSSO surveys, Health surveys etc.
description: Revision of basic sampling techniques; small area estimation, sampling for rare population, network sampling, quota and cluster sampling with practical examples from NSSO, health and other large-scale surveys.

title: Data Mining Techniques and Data Analysis
description: Basic concepts of data mining including data understanding, preparation, modeling, evaluation and deployment; anomaly detection, association rule learning, neural nets, machine learning, data warehousing and data interoperability.

title: Training on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
description: Comprehensive training on artificial intelligence and machine learning concepts and applications, including ML modelling approaches relevant to official statistics.

title: Current Economic Issues
description: Global economic scenario and current macro-economic scenario in India; WTO negotiations and impact on India; development economics, global financial crisis, environment economics and carbon trading, and outsourcing issues.

title: Induction Training Programme for New Recruits - Subordinate Statistical Service (SSS)
description: Mandatory induction training for new SSS recruits covering basic statistical techniques and sample survey techniques, official statistics, office procedures, computer applications and FOD field training.

title: Sample Survey Methodology & Estimation
description: For ISS probationers: survey methodology and data analytics including designing, building, collecting, processing, analyzing, disseminating and evaluating data collected through surveys and census, referencing NSSO and NFHS surveys.

title: Official Statistics & Related Methodology (ISEC)
description: Course for international students of the International Statistical Education Centre (ISI, Kolkata) covering the statistical system, population, labour, agriculture, industrial, finance, price, social and national accounts statistics, and organization of large-scale surveys.

title: Official Statistics Awareness Programme for University Professors and PG Students
description: Awareness programme popularising official statistics among university faculty and PG students, designed to introduce official statistics at the PG level and promote interest in application of statistics in Government functioning.

slides.title: Importance of Training
bulletPoints: Training is one of the critical components in the framework of Human Resource Development.
Training enhances the efficiency, growth, quality of skill of new entrants and working employees as well.
Increasing the potential of human capital across statistical organizations.

slides.title: Mandate of NASA
bulletPoints: National Academy of Statistical Administration (NASA) established on 13th February, 2009.
Mandate: Training on official Statistics and related discipline to the statistical personnel of the Central/State Govt./PSU and neighbouring/developing countries.

slides.title: Vision of NASA
bulletPoints: To be a Centre of Excellence in imparting training on Official Statistics & Related Methodology and undertaking research activities thereto.

slides.title: Aims & Objective
bulletPoints: To strengthen the statistical system by creating trained manpower in theoretical and official statistics to manage data collection, compilation, analysis and dissemination.
To create a national pool of certified statistical trainers.
To facilitate and organize international training programmes for SAARC and developing nations.
To assess training needs and develop capacity development strategies for statistical personnel.
To promote and undertake research in official statistics.

slides.title: Type of Training Programmes
bulletPoints: Domestic: Induction Training Programmes, Refresher Training Programmes, Mandatory and Domain Specific Trainings.
Other Training Programmes: Need Based Programmes, Awareness Programmes, TOT programmes, and workshops.
International Training Programmes for global statistical officers.

slides.title: Induction Training Programmes
bulletPoints: Indian Statistical Service (ISS) Officers: 1.5 years academic and 6 months on the job training (total of 2 years).
Promotee officers from SSS cadre to Junior Time Scale of ISS: 6 weeks (2 weeks IT, 2 weeks official & basic statistics, 1 week office procedures, 1 week field visit).
Subordinate Statistical Personnel (SSS): 6-7 weeks (3 weeks at NASA, 3-4 weeks at Zonal Training Centres of FOD).

slides.title: Refresher Training Programmes
bulletPoints: Mandatory Programmes for ISS in-service Officers: On average 5 programmes annually.

Domain Specific Training Programmes: For ISS officers (at least 6 programmes), SSS officials (10 programmes of 1-week duration), and State Statistical Officers from DES (6 programmes of 1-2 weeks duration).

slides.title: Other Training Programmes
bulletPoints: Training Programme for M.Stat students of ISI: 3-week training on official statistics (1 week class room lectures and 2 weeks on project work).
Training Programmes for popularizing Official Statistics: 1-week programme on official statistics for Heads/Senior Professors of Departments of Statistics as TOT programme.

slides.title: Other Training Programmes (Contd)
bulletPoints: Two Training Programmes for PG Students on official Statistics (1-week duration).
At least 3 one-day workshops at University Campuses.
Organizing national seminars and technical symposiums.

slides.title: International Training Programmes
bulletPoints: International Statistics Education Centre (ISEC): 6-week training programme on Official Statistics & Related Methodology of ISEC participants as per requirement of ISI Kolkata/Delhi.
Need Based Training Programmes based on requests received from neighbouring or SAARC countries.

slides.title: Resource Persons & Collaborations
bulletPoints: Apart from regular faculty, NASA draws specialized faculty from various Ministries.
Invites senior professors from Universities, teaching and research institutions.
Collaborating institutions: IIMs, ISI, JNU, ASCI, IASRI, NIFM, IIPA, IIPS, Labour Bureau, VV Giri National Labour Institute.

slides.title: Areas of Training: Core Statistics
bulletPoints: Demography & Population studies.
Index Numbers, Concept of Composite Index, Development Indices.
Sample Survey Methodology and designs (focus on NSSO surveys).
Data Processing: Validation, imputation of missing data, analysis and preparation of survey reports.
Statistical Methods & Applied Econometrics (ARIMA, ARCH, GARCH with SPSS/STATA/E-Views).

slides.title: Areas of Training: Official Statistics
bulletPoints: Fundamentals of Official Statistical System in India.
System of official statistics: Agriculture, Census, Irrigation, Industry, Education, Labour, Health, MDG.
Financial Statistics: Insurance, Taxation, Banking, Trade, Balance of Payments.
System of National Accounts and Indian Budgeting Process.

slides.title: Areas of Training: IT Related
bulletPoints: Basic IT Module: MS Office, Internet & RDBMS.
Advanced Training in IT: C++, Oracle, .NET, ASP.NET, Visual Basic.
Module on the use of IT Tools: SPSS, STATA, SAS, R software.

slides.title: Areas of Training: Other Related Subjects
bulletPoints: Basics of Micro and Macro Economic Theory and its interpretation.
Monetary and Fiscal Policy Concepts and understanding current economic policies.
Basic Modern Management Practices with case studies.
Application of Geographic Information System (GIS) & Remote Sensing.

slides.title: NASA - Achievements
bulletPoints: No. of Trainees (2009-10): 1,066 trainees.
No. of Trainees (2010-11): 1,068 trainees across 65 programmes.
No. of Trainees (2011-12): 1,400 trainees across 61 programmes.
No. of Trainees (2012-13): 1,500 trainees across 55 programmes.
NASA conducted 15 International Training Programmes during 2012-13.

slides.title: International Training / Workshops (2012-13)
bulletPoints: Data Analysis and Report Writing using STATA for Afghanistan participants.
National Accounts Statistics and Price Statistics for Afghanistan CSO officers.
Planning and Designing of Sample Survey followed by 1-week field attachment.
Agriculture & Gender Statistics using GIS for SAARC participants.
Demography & Population studies for DCS Sri Lanka and Maldives.

slides.title: Recent Initiatives
bulletPoints: Internship Scheme for University Students.
Revision of Course Curriculum & preparation of Training Manuals.
Training Courses for Heads of Department and Students of Statistics from Universities.
Assessment of Training Needs (TNA).
Participation with international and regional statistical organisations.

slides.title: Infrastructure Facilities at NASA
bulletPoints: Apex statistical training academy situated in Knowledge Park II, Greater Noida.
Comprehensive integrated campus with world-class academic, administrative, and residential facilities.
Dedicated power backup, high-speed campus network, and modern teaching aids.

slides.title: Academic Block
bulletPoints: Centrally Air-conditioned Auditorium with all digital and sound system (160 persons).
Conference Hall (60 persons).
5 Lecture/Seminar Halls with electronic modern teaching equipment and computer facilities.
Sukhatme Library equipped with extensive IT facilities.
Full-fledged Cafeteria and 24-hr power backup.

slides.title: Hostel / Residential Block
bulletPoints: Hostel Block: 40 single, 30 double bedded AC rooms (Total Capacity: 100 persons).
6 VIP suites / Guest Rooms for visiting dignitaries and international faculty.
Air-conditioned Dining Hall, Lounge with TV and entertainment facilities.
Facilities for indoor and outdoor games, Yoga Centre, Gym.
Residential Block: 20 residential quarters for officers & staff.

slides.title: Way Forward
bulletPoints: NASA is organizing training on official statistics to other in-service officers (IAS, IFS, IA&AS, IRS etc.).
NASA will bring out an Annual Journal on Official Statistics.
Setting up research and consultancy wings to enhance research activities.
Enhancing infrastructure facilities to accommodate more national and international training programmes.
